# Bumps that a person should look at before they merge themselves, because they
# could change the numbers in the three committed chain CSVs under data/.
#
# The sessions load those chains as the posterior instead of regenerating them,
# and regenerating is a cluster job: generate_pmcmc_seitl.jl and
# generate_pmcmc_seit4l.jl take many hours at 256 particles against CI's six
# hour limit. Nothing checks the committed draws against the versions that
# produced them, so this list is the only thing standing between a bump and an
# auto-merge. One workflow reads it: compathelper_automerge.yml.
#
# Note what a widened bound does and does not do. The version the code loads is
# the one pinned in Manifest.toml, which a widened bound leaves valid, so
# Pkg.resolve keeps it until someone re-resolves. A bump is the permission for a
# later move rather than the move itself, and the render that gates it installs
# the version already pinned. Catching the move needs a check that compares the
# manifest, which is not in place.
#
# This list is a judgement, not a derivation. Three rounds of trying to state a
# rule that picks it out produced a rule that either admitted most of the
# dependency tree or drew a line it could not defend. So it is maintained by
# hand, it is not exhaustive, and it errs towards holding a bump back: the cost
# of a wrong inclusion is one manual merge, and the cost of a wrong omission is
# a set of committed draws that no longer reproduce.
#
# One bare name per line, nothing else on the line: the reader matches the whole
# line with grep -qxF. Every name is a direct dependency, which is the right
# universe because the guard reads a CompatHelper title and CompatHelper bumps
# only those. Why each is here:
#
#   Turing                 drives sample()
#   AdvancedMH             RobustAdaptiveMetropolis, the proposal itself
#   SSMProblems            the state space model interface
#   GeneralisedFilters     BF, the bootstrap filter the chains run through
#   LogExpFunctions        softmax and logsumexp, which GeneralisedFilters
#                          weights and resamples with
#   JumpProcesses          the stochastic simulator, and the solve it runs on
#   DifferentialEquations  shares the SciMLBase stack that solve resolves
#                          against, so its bound moves what the jumps run on
#   Distributions          the priors and the observation model
#   ForwardDiff            ForwardDiff.value strips the Duals inside the PMMH
#                          model at scripts/pmmh_setup.jl:79
#
# LogExpFunctions is here for what GeneralisedFilters does with it, not for
# anything in this repository: logsumexp is called only by
# src/threaded_bootstrap_filter.jl, and the chains take the unthreaded BF path.
# Do not prune it on a grep of src/, which is what that evidence looks like.
#
# Deliberately absent, so these are not rediscovered as omissions:
#
#   Plots, StatsPlots           they draw the committed deck figures, which a
#                               script redraws in minutes. Only the chains are
#                               expensive, and only they are guarded here.
#   CSV, DataFrames,            they serialise the chains. A change there fails
#   FlexiChains                 the render rather than moving a draw.
#   StatsBase                   no route to the draws: wsample is imported at
#                               src/MFIIDD.jl:11 and never called, and
#                               GeneralisedFilters' resamplers.jl holds no
#                               StatsBase reference. Its one call in a
#                               generation script sets a histogram axis limit
#                               in a model-checking figure.
#   AdvancedVI                  nothing committed comes from it.

Turing
AdvancedMH
SSMProblems
GeneralisedFilters
LogExpFunctions
JumpProcesses
DifferentialEquations
Distributions
ForwardDiff
